events.turns_on: The white rabbit pin on Dujour's jacket — the planted symbol that converts an ordinary disk deal into an abduction-by-invitation and flips Neo from refusal to agreement the moment he recognizes it.

events.title: Neo's ordinary life reasserts itself
events.summary: The night's pull collapses into a mundane morning: an alarm clock drags Neo awake in his apartment, and he strains to read the clock-face, sees 9:15 A.M., and curses. The setting is then identified as the downtown office of Meta CorTechs, where Rhineheart lectures him about lateness and authority and delivers an either-or ultimatum about his job, to which Neo replies with flat, deferential compliance. The vast question Trinity raised is not answered or abandoned but crowded out by the immediate demand of the reprimand; he carries it still, pushed to the background by the mundane pressure of the workplace.

What he is late for
Whether any character is meant to be present in the skyscraper establishing shot, since none appears in the text
The time of day, which the skyscraper scene does not specify
Whether Neo's 'Perfectly clear' reflects genuine compliance or concealed resentment
Whether Rhineheart intends to fire Neo immediately if he is late again, or merely to warn him

affects_outside.enables: By pinning Neo to his desk under threat of losing his job, the ultimatum sets the terms for what follows: his failure to meet it becomes the ordinary-world pretext that lets outside forces trace and reach him.
affects_outside.blocks_or_costs: It costs Neo the momentum of the night before — the willing pull toward the answer offered to him is stalled, crowded out by the demand that he conform and be on time.
affects_outside.off_screen_reactor: The woman who sent him toward the question is absent here; her promise that the answer would find him goes unanswered while Neo submits to the ordinary world.

events.turns_on: The ordinary world reasserting its claim over Neo just as he is being pulled toward the truth — the pivot is whether the vast question or the small demand wins the morning, and for now the small demand does, so that Neo's 'Perfectly clear' is the price of moving through this world untouched.

events.title: The Agents seize Neo at the office
events.summary: A routine package delivers a ringing phone and Morpheus's warning that forces are closing in, and the abstract threat becomes a real raid. Guided turn-by-turn by Morpheus's voice, Neo moves across the office floor — into an empty cubicle, down a row, into a first office on the left — and slips past the searching Agents to the base of the skyscraper, only to be driven to a window ledge he cannot bring himself to cross. When his nerve breaks and he climbs back inside, the way out is gone; a female employee points out his position, and the Agents take him, handcuffed and forced into a dark sedan.

Who 'they' are beyond the Agents and cops seen in the neighbouring scene.

affects_outside.off_screen_reactor: Morpheus, having guided Neo to the ledge and handed him the choice, is now cut off — his voice gone with the dropped phone, unable to reach Neo in custody. Whatever larger plan he has been 'looking for' Neo to serve is now forced onto a harder, riskier path

events.turns_on: Neo's nerve at the window ledge — the one place where belief, not knowledge or guidance, is what is required, and the one thing he cannot summon. The escape succeeds until the crossing demands that he trust the impossible; the wind and the loss of the phone break his commitment, and his retreat back

events.title: Neo is interrogated and implanted
events.summary: The Agents close in on Neo in the interrogation room. Smith lays out Neo's two lives and offers to wipe his record clean in exchange for Morpheus; Neo refuses with contempt, insults Smith, and demands his phone call. Smith drops the negotiation, asking what good a phone call is if Neo cannot speak, and Neo's mouth seals shut and melds smooth. The other Agents pin him down, and Smith animates a fiber-optic wire tap into an insect-fluke-worm creature that burrows into Neo's exposed navel.

affects_outside.enables: It establishes that the Agents can rewrite a human body and silence a prisoner at will, so any later resistance or escape has to answer the fact that Neo has been marked and penetrated from the inside.
affects_outside.blocks_or_costs: It closes off Neo's belief that rights-talk or refusal can protect him, and it makes his defiant 'no' the thing that costs him his bodily integrity rather than winning his freedom.
affects_outside.off_screen_reactor: Morpheus, who has been hunting this man as 'The One,' is left with a captured and violated asset whose cooperation can no longer be assumed, forcing any rescue to move against an enemy who has proven he can alter a body at will.

events.turns_on: The pivot is the moment Smith asks what good a phone call is if Neo cannot speak and then erases Neo's mouth — the instant persuasion becomes raw compulsion, Neo's leverage disappears, and the wire tap becomes the physical means of his coercion.

events.title: Neo is reclaimed and taken to Morpheus
events.summary: A ringing phone wakes Neo — mouthless, shirt torn open, an implanted creature burrowing inside him — and a voice names him 'the One' and demands a single 'Yes.' He walks to the Adams Street bridge in the pouring rain, where a car slides to a stop; inside, Switch holds him at gunpoint while Apoc drives and Trinity insists the restraint is 'for our protection. From you.' When Switch stops the car and lays down 'Our way or the highway,' Neo opens the door to bolt, but Trinity reframes his flight as a road he has already been down and where it ends, and he closes the door and stays. The car then rushes off through the dark, wet streets, Neo half-dressed and rain-soaked, handed over to a war he has just consented to enter.

What exactly awaits Neo at the Adams Street bridge, or what 'meeting' Morpheus offers entails.

The exact nature of the 'road' Trinity says Neo already knows and where it ends.
Whether Apoc speaks at all or only drives.

affects_outside.enables: Neo's '... Yes' and his choice to close the car door put him in the crew's hands, clearing the way for the bug-extraction and his unplugging from the Matrix to follow.
affects_outside.blocks_or_costs: It ends Neo's ordinary life as a free hacker — he has consented, in fear, to be taken — and it commits Morpheus's cell to acting on faith in a man who still believes he is 'nobody,' with no way back to the life he knew.
affects_outside.off_screen_reactor: The Agents, who reached Neo first and now lose their quarry to Morpheus's crew; and Morpheus himself, waiting beyond these scenes to receive the One he has spent his life searching for.

events.turns_on: The pivot is Neo's choice to close the car door — the moment a resisting captive becomes a voluntarily compliant one who chooses to remain. Everything before it is coercion; everything after is consequence.

events.title: The Bug Removed
events.summary: In the moving car, Trinity seals an extractor over Neo's navel and, when suction alone fails to dislodge the tracker, she drives an electric charge through him to force it out; the fluke-like bug rockets through the coils into the glass cage, then reverts to a common wire tap when she tips it out onto the pavement behind the car, which carries on through the rain before halting in the alley behind Hotel Lafayette.

carried_uncertainty.what: Whether the discarded tracker fully reverts to an inert wire tap or still carries a traceable signal before it dies.
Whether Neo's body carries lasting harm from the current beyond the immediate shock.

affects_outside.enables: With the tracker gone, the crew can carry Neo to the hotel and on to the real world without the machines tracing the signal back to their ship.
affects_outside.blocks_or_costs: The discarded wire tap can no longer feed anyone Neo's location, but Neo has now paid for that with a brutal, violating procedure that hardens his fear even as it proves the crew's world is real.
affects_outside.off_screen_reactor: The Operators watching the bug's signal on the Nebuchadnezzar see it drop the moment the tracker is pulled, and Cypher's line goes quiet as the feed dies.

events.turns_on: The point where suction alone cannot dislodge the tracker and Trinity escalates to an electric charge, so that forcing the bug out of Neo means hurting him.

events.title: The Red Pill
events.summary: Trinity brings Neo to room 1313 and warns him to be honest with the one who knows everything, then hands him off. Inside, Morpheus reframes Neo's lifelong, nameless dread as a real enslaving system and offers him a choice between forgetting and knowing; Neo swallows the red pill. The crew wires the trace program to him, and as they race to lock his location, the cracked oval dressing mirror liquefies and crawls into his body until he goes into cardiac arrest, at which moment Apoc secures the target and Morpheus calls for the signal that drags Neo out of the Matrix.

affects_outside.enables: Neo's choice and unplugging put him on the ship and into the real war, where he can be shown what Morpheus believes he is; the extraction is the necessary precondition for everything that follows.
affects_outside.blocks_or_costs: The red pill closes off the blue-pill return to ordinary life — there is 'no going back' — and it costs Neo his body's safety, nearly killing him before the lock lands.
affects_outside.off_screen_reactor: The Oracle, if 'He' is the one Trinity meant, now has a recruit delivered to Morpheus on the strength of a warning given in his name; and Tank, summoned for the signal, must act on a call he did not originate.

events.turns_on: Neo swallowing the red pill rather than the blue one — the moment that converts a reversible seduction into an irreversible extraction and makes the catastrophe of unplugging earned rather than inflicted.

events.title: Born Into the Real World
events.summary: In cardiac arrest, Neo ruptures the magenta amnion and stands bald and naked in the oval capsule of clear alloy, mirror gel crawling over his face. A machine severs the coaxial cable at the base of his skull and the clear plastic needle and cerebrum-chip, then vacuums him through the black hole into the waste line, where he slides through the sewer main and nearly drowns before a metallic cable snatches him up into a flying machine. Lowered onto the hovercraft floor half-conscious, he is helped up to face Morpheus, who names him Neo and welcomes him to the real world, and then he passes out.

affects_outside.blocks_or_costs: His body has been flushed out of the pod and disconnected, so there is no going back to the life he had; the machine has lost him as a battery and the crew has taken on a half-dead recruit they must revive.

events.turns_on: The moment Neo is hauled from the waste flow into the flying machine and set before Morpheus — the pivot from being farmed to being free, sealed by Morpheus naming him Neo in the real world.

events.title: Waking and Rebuilding
events.summary: Neo is recovered aboard the Nebuchadnezzar and brought back to consciousness, where Morpheus—certain they have found the one—has his body rebuilt and then begins dismantling his assumptions about himself and his era, leading him out to witness the reality rather than describe it.

carried_uncertainty.what: Whether Trinity is physically present in the hovercraft or only heard as a voice.
How much time has passed since Neo passed out in sc-034.

affects_outside.enables: It puts a living, rebuilt Neo in front of Morpheus, so the crew can now move from saving his body to showing him the reality his mind still cannot conceive.
affects_outside.blocks_or_costs: It commits Morpheus to the strategy of showing over telling, closing off the gentler path of gradual explanation and setting up the violent resistance that full revelation will provoke.
affects_outside.off_screen_reactor: Trinity, whose doubt Morpheus overrode, is left holding the caution his certainty dismissed — the wariness that will matter if his faith in Neo proves misplaced.

events.turns_on: Morpheus's certainty that they have found the right man, which lets him manage Neo's awakening by doling out just enough truth to keep him calm while deferring the rest—showing rather than explaining, and treating Neo's terror as a stage to be guided through rather than soothed.

events.title: The Desert of the Real
events.summary: Morpheus leads Neo up a ladder to the main deck of the Nebuchadnezzar, then jacks him into the Construct and walks him through the truth of the Matrix: the world he knew is only a simulation, the sky was scorched, and humans are farmed for power. Neo resists every step, recoiling from the crew's touch as he comes to see them as agents of an unbearable violation, and when his mind cannot hold the truth his body speaks it — he thrashes against the restraints, tears free of the chair, screams at Trinity, Dozer, and Cypher to get away, then vomits and blacks out on the deck while the crew holds and tends him.

affects_outside.enables: Neo now carries the full truth of the Matrix and the human battery-farms, the knowledge every freed mind must hold before training can begin — the ground on which Morpheus will build the prophecy and the fight.
affects_outside.blocks_or_costs: Neo's peaceful ignorance is gone for good; the revelation breaks him physically and sets him on the path of despair and rejection that must be worked through before he can accept his role.
affects_outside.off_screen_reactor: The rest of the Nebuchadnezzar crew — Switch, Tank, and those not at the extraction — absorb a new, violently unsteady member whose first act on waking was to fight them off.

events.turns_on: The moment Morpheus holds up the coppertop battery and Neo refuses to believe it — the point where revelation stops being information and becomes an assault the mind cannot survive, so the body rejects it instead.

events.title: The Prophecy and the First of the Crew
events.summary: Recovered but spent, Neo lies awake in his dark room and accepts there is no going back; Morpheus enters, reframes the rescue as destiny by recounting the myth of the One and the Oracle's prophecy, then declares 'the search is over' before committing to guide him into training. Darkness gives way to flickering fluorescent light sticks in the hovercraft. Tank then enters as Neo's operator, shakes his hand, and — when Neo registers the missing jacks — explains that he and Dozer were born free in Zion, the last human city.

affects_outside.enables: The training to come — Tank's 'let's get to it' and Morpheus's 'Your training' put an operator in place and a recruit being oriented, so the Dojo, the jump program, and every subsequent test can begin.
affects_outside.blocks_or_costs: Neo's last door to his old life is closed ('No. But if you had the chance, would you truly choose it?'), so any path back to the life he knew is now foreclosed rather than merely difficult.
affects_outside.off_screen_reactor: Cipher, whose later betrayal runs against the trust Tank here builds — Neo is being taught to see the crew as safe, a lesson Cipher will exploit from within.

events.turns_on: Morpheus's declaration that 'the search is over' — the moment he stops apologizing for the rule he broke and commits, as a true believer, to the idea that Neo is the prophesied One.

events.title: The Sparring Program
events.summary: Tank skips the prescribed basics and loads combat programs straight into Neo, who absorbs kung fu and jujitsu in hours and comes out of the download convinced he now knows how to fight. Morpheus arrives, refuses to celebrate the claim, and submits it to a physical test in the dojo. Across a series of spars, Neo's furious, technique-driven assault is blocked and dismantled every time, until Morpheus beats him to the floor and insists that speed and even the air are not real forces — that this world answers to the mind, not the muscles. Neo's breakthrough comes not through understanding but through rage: he stops trying to perform technique and simply lands one clean blow on Morpheus, knocking his glasses off. Morpheus does not retaliate; he stops the spar and reframes himself as only a guide who can show the door, then orders Tank to load the jump program. The crew — Mouse, Tank and the rest — watch from the main deck as a spectacle, reading the fight's physiological signatures and confirming from the outside that what Neo is doing should not be possible.

affects_outside.off_screen_reactor: The crew on the main deck — Mouse and the others — abandon dinner and crowd the monitors, gasping at the impossible neural-kinetics; their off-screen astonishment is the story's external confirmation that Neo is exceeding every expectation.

events.title: The Jump
events.summary: Morpheus moves the session to a rooftop jump program to prove that the mind, not physics, governs the Construct, and crosses the gap himself to set the example. Neo runs and falls badly short, the yielding ground catching him, and on the main deck the crew watches the attempt split between doubters and believers while Trinity's quiet hope breaks her reserve and then she leaves before the aftermath. Tank seizes the disk and eases the plug from Neo, who is returned to his body injured, groaning, cradling his ribs and spitting blood into his hand. Morpheus guides Neo to name his own disbelief as the cause, then delivers the lethal corollary.
participants: the blood Neo spits into his hand

carried_uncertainty.what: Whether Morpheus's nod means Neo has fully learned the lesson or merely named part of it.

affects_outside.enables: Neo now carries the operational rule that mind governs the Construct, the foundation every later feat (the rooftop leaps, and eventually stopping sentinels) is built on, and the lethal corollary that frames every future jacking as genuinely mortal.
affects_outside.blocks_or_costs: The failure, and Switch's insistence that it means nothing, shut down the room's open hope and harden the crew's split; it also feeds Cypher's conviction that the prophecy is a con, tightening the resentment he will act on.
affects_outside.off_screen_reactor: No new off-screen reactor is established here; Trinity's departure is on-screen, and the scene layer records no response from anyone outside these scenes.

events.turns_on: The pivot is Neo's failure itself: only by falling short does the abstract doctrine become a lived, bodily truth, and only the pain, the blood in his palm, and the plug eased out make him believe that the mind makes the Matrix real and that death there is death.

events.title: After Hours
events.summary: Trinity comes out of Neo's room having just been alone with the unconscious Neo in a way she can't own, and runs straight into Cypher watching her; she deflects his needling about her feelings without denying anything and leaves on her own terms, while Cypher—dressing up resentment over the dinner as a joke—fails to rattle her and reaches for the Oracle as a way to force Morpheus's faith into something verifiable, the first step away from loyalty.

whether Trinity's feelings are romantic or simply protective

affects_outside.off_screen_reactor: Morpheus, whose certainty Cypher is now quietly moving to put on trial, has no part in the exchange yet is its real target.

events.turns_on: A private, off-guard attachment to the unconscious Neo is converted into a guarded, denied-then-deflected secret the moment Cypher puts a skeptical witness on it—and his failure to rattle Trinity turns the probe from a sneer into a strategic lever aimed at Morpheus's faith.

events.title: The Agent training program
events.summary: On a crowded downtown street that turns out to be a training program, Morpheus moves effortlessly through the jostling crowd while Neo is bumped and shouldered off the path, and reframes the ordinary people around them as the enemy. He stops the simulation around a gun-levelled Agent, leaving everything else frozen, and uses it to teach that Agents are sentient programs who can move into anyone still hardwired to the system. He tells Neo that every human who has fought one has died, but that Neo can surpass any Agent because their strength and speed are bound by rules while his are not.

carried_uncertainty.what: Whether Neo can actually trust Morpheus's central promise that he will surpass the Agents — the scene offers it as faith, not verified fact.

affects_outside.enables: Neo now has the rules — Agents are sentient programs in anyone still plugged in, and they must eventually be fought — that the rest of the film will test, and Morpheus has set the terms for the bullet-dodging and rooftop training to come.
affects_outside.blocks_or_costs: It shuts down Neo's remaining view of the Matrix as a benign or neutral place, recasting every ordinary face as a potential enemy, and it loads him with the knowledge that fighting an Agent has killed everyone who tried — a burden Morpheus places on him before
affects_outside.off_screen_reactor: Tank, reporting 'trouble' over Morpheus's cell phone, interrupts the lesson from off-screen, signalling that something has gone wrong on the ship while this training ran.

events.turns_on: The program freezing on Morpheus's command — the moment the street reveals itself as a construct and the gun-levelled Agent becomes a lesson about sentient programs and rule-bound power rather than a death.

events.title: The Sentinel hunt and the ship's hiding
events.summary: A Sentinel sweeping the sewer main forces the Nebuchadnezzar into a tiny supply line too small for it, where Tank kills power and arms the E.M.P. as the ship's only weapon. The crew goes cold and silent, frozen in the darkened cockpit while the machine glides directly over them, then breathes again once it passes and disappears.

Whether Tank is physically present in the cockpit or elsewhere on the ship.

events.title: Cypher's disillusionment and his deal
events.summary: On the Nebuchadnezzar's main deck, Cypher pours Dozer's liquor for Neo and recasts Morpheus's prophecy as a body count, telling him five before him took on an Agent and died because Morpheus got them believing. Neo takes it as caution and retreats toward the ladder, shaken rather than converted. Cypher then crosses into the Matrix to a restaurant, where he savors an impossible steak and strikes a bargain with Agent Smith: his body returned to a power plant and reinserted as someone rich, important, and forgetful, in exchange for delivering the man who holds Zion's mainframe access codes. Smith names that man as Morpheus, and Cypher's private regret settles into reconciled treason.

events.title: The crew goes in to reach the Oracle

Tank launches the jump, and the crew materializes in the Hotel Lafayette before stepping back into the Matrix. As the others move toward the car, Cypher covertly connects a phone and drops it in a garbage can in the alley. During the drive, Neo grapples with the falseness of his memories and presses Trinity about what the Oracle told her, but she is struck physically mute at the moment of disclosure.

events.title: Entering the building and meeting the Oracle
events.summary: The party arrives at a vast tenement-like building understood as a place where people can disappear. Morpheus leads Neo up through it, into the elevator, down the hall, and to the Oracle's apartment door, while Neo follows and, at the threshold, backs away before committing. During the ascent, Neo presses Morpheus over the five failed candidates, and Morpheus confesses that he misunderstood the Oracle — that he had believed the prophecy was all about him and that he could anoint whoever he chose — admitting he was terribly wrong. He shifts from describing the Oracle in the abstract to disclosing that she personally told him he would find the One, and asks Neo to lean on residual respect and trust him until Neo can feel what he feels. Neo learns the Oracle is a fallible-sounding guide who knows enough rather than everything, and, among the Potentials, accepts the Spoon Boy's lesson that bending the spoon is impossible because there is no spoon — only oneself bends, the truth that reality here is a projection of the self, confirmed as he stares into the spoon and the reflected room slowly begins to bend. The Priestess opens the door before Neo touches it, greets him by name, and shepherds him through the household to the Oracle. Neo steps through the door into the Oracle's apartment, called forward to meet her while Morpheus is left behind, suspended between the terror of being the One and the safety of being a nobody.

events.title: The crew watches as Neo decides to stand and fight
events.summary: Aboard the ship's Main Deck, Morpheus, Trinity and Tank watch the scrolling code while Neo stands alone in the subway station before a dead escalator. Trinity, having been brought back aboard from the rooftop, urges Neo to run; Neo does not run. He turns back from the escalator to face the hunter and hardens into a fixed, gunfighter's calm. On the deck, Morpheus reads that stillness as the beginning of belief, while Trinity can only register it as something she cannot understand.

carried_uncertainty.what: Whether Neo can hear or obey Trinity's command
What has happened to Neo to make running necessary
The exact nature of the scrolling code they are watching

affects_outside.enables: Neo's decision to stand rather than run sets him on the path to the confrontation that follows, where that same belief will be tested to the breaking.
affects_outside.blocks_or_costs: It closes off the escape Trinity is trying to force, committing Neo to a fight he cannot yet win and leaving the crew powerless to reach him.
affects_outside.off_screen_reactor: Agent Smith, waiting in the station, now faces a Neo who has stopped fleeing and turned to meet him.

events.turns_on: Neo's stillness — his refusal to run and his decision to turn and face the hunter — which Trinity reads as something she cannot understand and Morpheus reads as the first sign that Neo is beginning to believe he is the One.

events.title: Neo and Smith's subway battle; Neo seizes his power and runs
events.summary: After their gunfight ends in a mutual empty click, Neo and Agent Smith trade bare-handed blows until Smith chokes Neo near the electrified third-rail and uses the arriving train to frame his death as settled inevitability; at the edge of death Neo refuses the name and fate Smith pronounces, summons an impossible surge, hurls Smith into the tunnel ceiling, and breaks free as the train barrels over him—only for Smith to burst from the last car, glasses intact, and resume the chase as Neo runs, limping, for the escalator.

carried_uncertainty.what: Whether either combatant gains a lasting advantage, since the fight ends with Smith attacking with unrelenting fury and the outcome unresolved.
The meaning of Smith's eyes turning 'ice blue' beyond what the text literally shows.
Whether the train physically injures Agent Smith or merely interrupts him, since he emerges moments later unharmed with his glasses intact.
Whether Neo's surge of strength is self-generated or caused by any external force; the text only says 'Impossibly.'

affects_outside.enables: Neo's refusal and impossible surge prove to both combatants that he is no longer a fixed quantity, setting the terms for the death-and-rebirth beat that follows and for Smith's determination to delete him in the hotel.
affects_outside.blocks_or_costs: Neo's escape is only a change of shape, not a victory: by running for the escalator he runs toward the hotel hallway where Smith will ambush and shoot him, so the flight costs him the illusion of getting away.
affects_outside.off_screen_reactor: Tank, who has blocked Trinity from re-entering the Matrix, now watches through her what Smith is doing to Neo—confirming on the ship that the anomaly is being killed and tightening the pressure toward the extraction that must follow.

events.turns_on: The pivot is Neo's refusal of the name and fate Smith imposes—'My name is Neo'—spoken at the instant of his apparent death, which converts him from a man fighting the rules into one who stops obeying them and unleashes the impossible surge; it is also the moment Smith's certainty that Neo is a fixed

events.title: The Crew Lose Neo and the Sentinels Arrive
events.summary: In the hovercraft, Tank loses Neo on the screen. A siren sounds; Morpheus, who had begun interpreting events for the crew, breaks off and bolts for the ladder into the cockpit. There he reads the sentinels on the radar, gives the crew five or six minutes, and orders Tank to charge the E.M.P. Tank, who had lost the feed, converts his alarm into pure compliance and charges the weapon. Trinity, having just watched Neo's body jerk and cough blood, moves into the cockpit behind Morpheus and objects that Neo must be out before the E.M.P. is used; Morpheus answers 'I know, Trinity' and reassures her that Neo will make it.

carried_uncertainty.what: What the siren is warning about.
Whether Morpheus reaches the ladder or why he goes there.
Whether Neo will make it back before the E.M.P. must be used.

affects_outside.enables: The E.M.P. charge puts the ship's only defense on a timer, so that when Neo is ambushed and shot moments later, the crew's ability to save him is now boxed in by a countdown that did not exist before this event.
affects_outside.blocks_or_costs: It forecloses any unhurried reckoning with what happened to Neo inside the Matrix; his fate is subordinated to the sentinels' approach, and Trinity's need for an answer about whether he is alive is left deliberately unanswered.
affects_outside.off_screen_reactor: Neo, still jacked in and fleeing toward an exit, is the unseen party the whole deadline is measured against — the order to charge the E.M.P. turns his flight into a race he does not know he is running.

events.turns_on: Whether the E.M.P. can be made ready without being fired on Neo before he is out — and whether Morpheus's faith that Neo will make it is right.

events.title: Neo's Flight Through the City to the Fire Escape
events.summary: Neo snatches the BUSINESSMAN's cell phone mid-sprint and raises the crew, then runs a gauntlet that tightens at every block: his call becomes a demand for extraction, the demand becomes a running report as Smith closes to point-blank range, the open market fills with Agents at every turn, and a dead-end alley forces him to kick his way through an apartment building while Tank steers him by voice. He breaks a locked door, gets redirected twice, dives through a window as a knife pins the casing, drops down a fire escape, and lands broken and bleeding, still not out.

carried_uncertainty.what: Whether the bullet in the alley hits Neo or only shatters his mirror-image.
How far ahead of Smith Neo is when Smith opens fire.
Whether anyone answers Neo's cry for help in the dead-end alley.
The exact time of day.
Whether the two women in the apartment notice or react to Neo passing through.
The identity of the pursuers firing the bullets and throwing the knife (implied Agents, not named in the scene).
Whether Neo reaches the end of the alley or Agent Brown catches him.
The time of day at the fire escape.

affects_outside.enables: Tank locating the exit and steering Neo to the fire escape keeps the extraction live, so the crew's one defense—the EMP—can still be held until Neo is out rather than detonated with him still inside.
affects_outside.blocks_or_costs: The chase burns the clock and leaves Neo broken and bleeding with Agent Brown a breath behind, narrowing the window before the Sentinels force the EMP's use and raising the cost of any further delay.
affects_outside.off_screen_reactor: Morpheus, who ordered the EMP charge and must decide whether to fire it, is reacting off-screen to every second Neo stays in; the Agents inside the Matrix are coordinating the hunt that has now cornered their target.

events.turns_on: Whether Neo reaches the routed fire-escape phone before the Agents close the trap.

events.title: Recognition and the Sentinel Ambush
events.summary: Two recognitions land at once. Across from the Heart O' The City Hotel, Agent Smith is passing when the place suddenly registers with him and his focus locks onto its faded neon sign, fixing him at the point of identification without yet acting. Aboard the Nebuchadnezzar in the sewer main, Tank loads the exit and commits to making the call while Morpheus drives the escape — but the lights go red, the sentinels slam down onto the hull, and the ship passes in an instant from a refuge running an extraction to a vessel under direct physical assault, leaving Morpheus at the EMP detonator as the only move left.
participants: the faded NEON sign reading 'Heart O' The City Hotel'

carried_uncertainty.what: Whether Agent Smith recognizes the hotel because he senses Neo's presence there or for some other reason.
What Agent Smith intends to do after pausing, since the scene ends on the recognition.

affects_outside.enables: Smith's recognition of the hotel fixes the location where Neo is trying to surface, so the agents now have a place to converge on rather than a city to search. On the ship, Morpheus arming the EMP is the move that lets the crew answer the sentinel breach with
affects_outside.blocks_or_costs: The arrival of the pursuers closes the escape window Tank is rushing into, so the call he is about to make may not complete before the agents are on them — the extraction is arrested at its last second.
affects_outside.off_screen_reactor: Neo, out on the rooftop and already coughing blood with wild life-signs, is the one this turn is really about, yet he is not in these scenes; the crew's sudden shift from 'get him out' to 'they are here' happens entirely around his absence, and whatever he is

events.turns_on: The escape is arrested by the hunters' arrival: Tank and Morpheus are still driving the extraction forward when the red lights and the sentinels' strike convert the ship from refuge to target in a single beat, snapping the situation from 'will they get Neo out' to 'they are here' and leaving the EMP

events.title: Neo's Flight to the Phone
events.summary: Neo climbs a fire escape under fire in the alley while two Agents close the gap behind him; the chase cuts to a man breaking through a third-floor window into a hall, then to the hovercraft where Tank reports a hull breach and Trinity drives Neo to hurry, then back to the hall where Neo races toward door 303 and is stopped cold by Agent Smith's point-blank shot.

carried_uncertainty.what: The identity of the man in the hall — the scene only calls him 'he'.
Which direction he runs after entering the hall.
Whether the descending door numbers signal pursuers or merely his progress.
Whether Neo dies from the shot or survives.
Whether Neo reaches or answers the ringing phone.

affects_outside.enables: The hull breach reported here forces the crew toward extraction, setting up the push to get Neo and Morpheus out before the ship is overrun.
affects_outside.blocks_or_costs: Neo's shot at door 303 removes his clean escape through the phone and leaves him exposed and down, costing the crew the time and the clean exit they were counting on.
affects_outside.off_screen_reactor: Morpheus, whose extraction now has to happen under a collapsing margin he cannot see from the hovercraft scenes.

events.turns_on: The exit Neo sprints toward — door 303 — has already been turned into the ambush, so his momentum toward it delivers him into Agent Smith's hands: the shot stops him cold and leaves him frozen and helpless.

events.title: Death, the Kiss, and the Miracle
events.summary: In the Matrix, Agent Smith shoots Neo three times in the chest in the hall and Agent Brown confirms him gone; in the real world, the life monitors flatline and the crew gives him up even as sentinels breach the hull. Trinity refuses the ending: she takes hold of his body and kisses him, and the monitors jump back to life. Neo's eyes snap open, and Morpheus, who had reached for the EMP in weeping despair, is left with his faith overturned.

carried_uncertainty.what: Whether Neo is actually dead or merely incapacitated when Smith shoots him and Brown confirms him.
Whether Neo is alive or dead at the moment Trinity takes hold of his body, since the scene does not state his condition.
Whether the destruction raining on the main deck is caused by the sentinels slicing the hull, as the scene does not specify the source.
Whether Neo actually responds to Trinity's kiss within the scene.
Whether Morpheus ultimately triggers the EMP switch.
Who 'He' is, since the scene gives no name.
Who 'they' are and what 'they do'.
What specific action 'He does' refers to.
Whether the monitors returning to life means Neo himself is reviving, before Trinity's command clarifies it.
Whether Tank and Morpheus share the same reaction when they look at each other.

affects_outside.enables: Neo's return from death is the event that confirms him as the One — the prophecy the crew has been betting on is no longer a hope but something they have watched happen. It also gives the ship a reason to keep fighting instead of firing the EMP and ending it.
affects_outside.blocks_or_costs: The Agents' certainty that the threat is over is now false, but so is any chance of the crew treating this as a clean victory — the sentinel breach means survival still hangs by a thread, and Morpheus's shattered faith cannot simply be restored by a miracle he
affects_outside.off_screen_reactor: The sentinels pressing the breach are the off-screen force driving the real-world peril; within the Matrix, the other Agents and the operators who rely on Neo's success react to a situation now fundamentally changed by a death that did not hold.

events.turns_on: Trinity's kiss — the moment she stops grieving and, staking everything on the Oracle's words, refuses to let the flatline be final. It is the hinge between the two declared deaths and the revival that undoes them.

events.title: The One Awakens
events.summary: Revived in the hotel hall, Neo halts the Agents' volley with a raised hand and begins reading the room as flowing code; aboard the Nebuchadnezzar the crew watches him blaze across the screens and Morpheus declares him the One, moments before an explosion rocks the ship; back in the hall Neo enters Agent Smith and bursts out of him, destroying the first Agent ever, so the surviving Agents feel fear for the first time and flee.

carried_uncertainty.what: Who or what caused the explosion aboard the Nebuchadnezzar.
Whether Trinity is among those who 'begin to blur into streaks' or only Tank and Morpheus.

affects_outside.enables: The surviving Agents' flight clears the hall and buys the crew a window, and Neo's new command of the Matrix sets the terms for every confrontation that follows — he now operates outside the rules the system relies on to catch him.
affects_outside.blocks_or_costs: The destruction of Smith removes one hunter but announces Neo as ungovernable, guaranteeing the system will send what adapts rather than what merely shoots; and the explosion aboard the Nebuchadnezzar ends the crew's celebration before it can settle into any安全
affects_outside.off_screen_reactor: The machines and whatever commands the Agents register, off-screen, that an Agent has been destroyed and that their prey has slipped their control — a loss their system cannot ignore.

events.turns_on: Neo's refusal of the bullets — the single raised hand that halts the volley and lets him see the world as code — is the pivot on which the whole event turns, because everything after (the Agents' fear, Smith's destruction, the crew's confirmation) follows from that one break in the rules.

events.title: The Escape
events.summary: Sentinels overrun the ship's main deck, jolting Trinity from awe at Neo's return into a single, urgent summons to get up. In a hall, a man who has only been hearing a woman's voice reacts to a ringing phone and charges toward its source. Back on the deck, a sentinel descends on Morpheus at the EMP switch; on a screen Neo appears as a rushing stream of code diving for the phone, and at Trinity's 'Now!'—timed to that dive—Morpheus turns the key. A searing burst of brilliant white light engulfs the chamber. overflow pit, and the sentinels blink and fall dead, their cold metal carcasses filling it.

carried_uncertainty.what: Whether Neo, Morpheus or Tank are present on the main deck in sc-219; only Trinity is named.
What Trinity wants Neo to do or know with her single call.
The identity of 'he' and 'her' in the hall scene.
What happens when he reaches the phone — the scene cuts off mid-action.
What turning the key does.
Whether Neo reaches the phone.
Whether the sentinel reaches Morpheus.
What produced the blinding shock of white light.
Whether that shock is connected to Neo diving for the phone in the neighbouring scenes.

affects_outside.enables: The destruction of the sentinels clears the ship long enough for the man in the hall to reach the ringing phone and for the crew to survive the assault, opening the way out of the hovercraft.
affects_outside.blocks_or_costs: The EMP-style surge that kills the sentinels spends the ship's last defense, leaving it powerless and still adrift over the real city, so the escape buys time at the cost of the vessel's ability to fight again.
affects_outside.off_screen_reactor: Tank and any crew not named on the deck neither appear nor react in these scenes; their fates during the sentinel assault are not shown here.

events.turns_on: The escape hinges on Trinity's 'Now!'—the instant she releases Morpheus's turn of the key in exact time with Neo's dive for the phone on the screen, the cue Morpheus waits for as the sentinel closes.

events.title: A New World
events.summary: In the darkened hovercraft, Trinity's vigil breaks: Neo wakes at her voice, reaches for her, and she weeps as she kisses him, releasing the grief she held while watching over his body. The scene then shifts to Neo standing alone in a hall, unharmed and transformed, before he moves into a phone booth on a city street and rises into open flight above the skyscrapers. Speaking from inside the Matrix, no longer running or hiding, he offers a choice between cage and chrysalis and describes a world beyond the one he used to see.

carried_uncertainty.what: Who exactly answers the ringing phone on the Matrix side, and whether Neo's audience is the machines, other plugged-in humans, or both.
Whether the hovercraft is moving, powered down, or in any particular state beyond 'still darkness.'

affects_outside.enables: Neo's broadcast into the Matrix opens a channel to any mind still plugged in, so others can now be reached and offered the same choice he took; his open declaration also means the machines know exactly where and who he is, removing the need for the chase that
affects_outside.blocks_or_costs: The fugitive phase is over, so the story can no longer run on hiding and pursuit; by choosing to be found, Neo gives up concealment as a strategy and commits to being seen, which closes off the safer, reactive path.
affects_outside.off_screen_reactor: Whoever is 'out there' in the Matrix—the machines or other plugged-in humans—now has to answer the choice Neo laid down, and their response falls outside these scenes.

events.turns_on: The pivot is Neo's transformation from private return to public declaration: the still darkness of the ship, where Trinity weeps over his living body, becomes, without a break, an address from inside the Matrix in which he stops being afraid of being found, reframes the world from cage to chrysalis,

entities.name: Neo (Thomas A. Anderson)
entities.kind: A dual-life man: by day a code-monkey at a respectable software firm, by night a black-market hacker selling illegal programs from his apartment.
entities.age_and_gender: A man in his early-to-mid thirties.
entities.appearance: Lean and pale from too many sleepless nights indoors; dark, close-cropped hair; a face that carries the hollow-eyed exhaustion of someone who has been staring at a glowing screen until dawn for years.
entities.clothing: Dresses in the anonymous uniform of a late-nineties office drone at work, then sheds it for long black coats and dark glasses once he steps into the underground.
entities.life_situation: Trapped in a gray, rule-bound day job he secretly despises while running an illicit software operation from a fortress-like apartment, all before being hunted by faceless government agents and pulled out of his old life entirely by a mysterious crew.
entities.key_relationships: Morpheus, the legendary figure who has spent his whole life hunting for him and names him 'the One'; Trinity, the hypnotic hacker whose riddling voice disarms him and who coaxes him to stay; Rhineheart, the boss who lectures him about a 'problem with authority'; and the Agents, the cold enforcers who hunt him without mercy.
entities.personality_big_five: Restless and inwardly rebellious beneath a mask of sullen compliance; curious to the point of obsession; capable of cocky, mocking defiance that can evaporate into raw terror in an instant; skeptical of his own worth, insisting he is 'nobody'; yet able to commit once something appeals to a deeper part of him.
entities.coping_with_problems: Retreats into detached, silent endurance and lets his attention drift away, then follows precise instructions from a steadier voice when the walls close in; swings between brash bravado and collapse when force is applied, and repeatedly backs away from anything that feels like certain death.
entities.dreams_and_goals_short: To finally learn the truth behind 'the Matrix,' the mystery that has consumed his sleepless nights, and to follow the white rabbit wherever it leads.
entities.goals_long_term: To stop feeling like a stranger in his own life and to become something more than a rule-following nobody, even if it means walking into the unknown.
entities.fears: That he will die trying something impossible, like leaping across a gap between rooftops; that he is being hunted for no reason he can understand; and the bottomless dread of losing control of his own body to something forced inside him.
entities.wanted_image_and_roles: Wants to be seen as a legendary hacker and a seeker of forbidden knowledge, not the obedient employee everyone expects; drawn toward the role of 'the One' even as it sickens and unsettles him.
entities.comfortable_feelings_vs_shadow: Finds comfort in the solitary, controlled dark of his apartment and the thrill of the hunt for answers; his shadow is the panic that floods him when a machine seems to act on its own will, or when his bravado is stripped away by physical force.
entities.intellect_and_skills: A gifted programmer and legendary hacker who chases elusive figures through code and runs a covert software business with layered locks and hidden compartments; learns fast under pressure and can execute turn-by-turn escape commands even while terrified.
entities.interests_hobbies: Hacking, chasing hacker legends and myths, and losing himself for endless nights in the puzzle of 'the Matrix,' an obsession he has never told a soul about.
entities.background_story: A solitary hacker who has spent years quietly obsessed with the mystery of 'the Matrix,' selling illegal disks from a heavily secured apartment while pretending to be a model employee at Meta Cortechs, until a knock that answered his last message and a series of escalating encounters with Morpheus, Trinity, and the Agents dragged him out of his double life.
entities.typical_sentences_style: Short, defensive, and skeptical, swinging from mocking sarcasm to frightened protest; questions authority with a sneer, then cracks into raw, honest fear when cornered.
entities.secrets_never_said: His years-long obsession with 'the Matrix' and the unknown figure he has chased through sleepless nights, something he has never shared with anyone, and the private terror of a machine that seemed to answer him with a will of its own.

entities.name: Trinity (also 'Trinity' as a hacker handle; initially believed by NEO to be a man)
entities.kind: Human; a freed human operative living inside a simulated reality while also existing in the real world aboard a hovercraft; a legendary figure in the hacker underground.
entities.age_and_gender: Adult woman, likely late twenties to early thirties; physically at peak condition.
entities.appearance: Clad in close-fitting black leather that moves with her like a second skin; a 'leather-clad ghost' whose speed and precision make armed, trained cops fail to register her as a threat until it is too late; carries herself with a calm, unreadable face even mid-leap between rooftops.
entities.clothing: Black leather clothing suited to combat and flight; practical, unadorned, built for movement rather than display.
entities.life_situation: A hunted fugitive operating inside a surveilled, rule-bound simulated world, moving from phone to phone as exits, always low on time and pursued by Agents; part of a small crew led by MORPHEUS and guided by an OPERATOR through a phone link; based in the real world aboard a hovercraft.
entities.key_relationships: Devoted to MORPHEUS and his search for 'the One' and 'the answer'; serves as guide, protector, and believer for NEO, staking her own judgment on his honesty; works alongside crewmates SWITCH (who favors brute force) and an OPERATOR who directs her exits; treats NEO as a genuine seeker worth investing in.
entities.personality_big_five: Extremely low in visible fear and high in composure under pressure; fiercely disciplined and self-regulating; decisive and action-first, though she can panic for an instant before forcing calm; coolly intimate and certain with those she trusts; willing to risk herself for a cause and for people she believes in; prefers gentle, personal persuasion over force when she can.
entities.coping_with_problems: When cornered she first reads the room — even feigning surrender — then explodes into precise, lethal violence the instant restraint becomes a trap; under extreme pressure she spikes into panic, curses, then deliberately breathes and forces herself calm with a clipped 'All right,' committing fully to the dangerous plan; when physically broken she gets back up and keeps moving; when out of options she takes desperate, self-endangering risks rather than be caught.
entities.dreams_and_goals_short: Escape the Agents by reaching a ringing phone before it is destroyed; extract tracking bugs and keep NEO alive through the extraction; deliver warnings and bring NEO safely to MORPHEUS.
entities.goals_long_term: See MORPHEUS's search fulfilled — the discovery of 'the One' and 'the answer' — a cause she has devoted herself to and now pins to NEO.
entities.fears: Being caught or traced by the Agents; failing the candidate she vouched for and watching his vitals fail; the possibility that her belief in NEO is misplaced.
entities.wanted_image_and_roles: Wants to be seen as the crew's cool, certain operative — guide, protector, and true believer — the legendary hacker whose name commands awe, and the one who recognizes and ushers in 'the One.'
entities.comfortable_feelings_vs_shadow: Comfortable in controlled, high-pressure moments where calm and precision win; in intimate, certain exchanges with a seeker she trusts. Her shadow is the split-second of raw panic and the terror of a cause collapsing — the moment vitals flatline and the person she bet on might die.
entities.intellect_and_skills: A highly trained, lethal close-quarters combatant who disarms and kills a full squad of armed cops in seconds; a superhumanly agile athlete capable of a roughly 40-foot rooftop leap and of diving through windows while protecting her head; medically and technically competent, performing a high-stakes bug extraction and reading clinical vitals under time pressure; a master of navigating the simulated world's phone-exit rules; a legendary hacker.
entities.interests_hobbies: Hacking and operating in the underground; high-speed motorcycle pursuit and urban flight; the disciplined craft of combat and escape.
entities.background_story: A legendary name in the hacker underground, once mistaken even by NEO as a man; freed from the simulated world and now part of MORPHEUS's crew, devoted to his search for 'the One' and 'the answer'; hunted by Agents, she moves through the simulated city by phone exits while based in the real world aboard a hovercraft, and she personally identifies and recruits NEO, staking her judgment on him.
entities.typical_sentences_style: Short, clipped, controlled; calm directive reassurance under pressure ('Lie back,' 'Try to relax,' 'All right'); cool, intimate certainty laced with cryptic warnings; persuasive rather than loud, leaning on trust and a person's own history instead of threats.
entities.secrets_never_said: The private weight of having staked her own judgment on NEO's honesty before MORPHEUS; the terror she swallows when his vitals fail and she must keep him alive; the depth of her devotion to the cause and to 'him' that she rarely voices outright; the ambiguous line between her feigned surrender and her real intent to kill.

entities.name: Morpheus (entity profile)
entities.kind: A veteran commander and recruiter of a hidden resistance who operates as both a remote field controller and a ceremonial guide for new recruits.
entities.age_and_gender: A mature man, well past his prime years, carrying the weight of a lifelong hunt.
entities.appearance: A tall, imposing figure with a still, unhurried bearing; his eyes read the readiness of others and his smile can light up a room when he chooses warmth over command.
entities.clothing: Dresses in dark, close-fitting garments suited to command posts and shipboard decks rather than any display of status.
entities.life_situation: Lives aboard a mobile resistance vessel, spending his days hunting for a prophesied liberator while running live operations against a surveillance state that traces every line.
entities.key_relationships: Trusts Trinity to execute dangerous physical runs and leans on her as his most capable field operative; treats Neo as the man he has hunted his whole life and the focus of his deepest conviction.
entities.personality_big_five: Radiates controlled certainty and speaks in a flat, low, unhurried register even under fire; warm and courteous when welcoming a recruit, yet refuses to soothe or over-explain, preferring to reframe fear as the only true obstacle.
entities.coping_with_problems: Compresses alarm beneath a hard shell of command, converts every threat into a movement order, and lends his own certainty to others so they can act while he works against a tracing clock.
entities.dreams_and_goals_short: Bring each recruit across the threshold safely—guiding a frightened man past a closing search, extracting a failing body, and delivering the temporal shock that ends the old life.
entities.goals_long_term: Find and confirm the One he has searched for his entire life, then free others by leading them to a truth they already half-know.
entities.fears: That fear, not incapacity, will hold a chosen man back from the right choice; that a traced line or a failing body will cost him the recruit before the crossing is complete.
entities.wanted_image_and_roles: Wants to be seen as the patient, certain guide who has performed this recruitment ritual many times and can be trusted to carry both the philosophy and the physical rescue in one motion.
entities.comfortable_feelings_vs_shadow: Most at ease in disciplined, almost ceremonial focus where certainty replaces hope; the shadow is the compressed alarm and vindicated reverence he keeps sealed beneath the commander's voice.
entities.intellect_and_skills: Reads an entire tactical situation at once, stays ahead of his operatives by knowing a line was traced before they report it, and times crew instructions around a subject's failing body with Socratic calm.
entities.interests_hobbies: Refines a recruitment ritual performed with patient certainty, redirecting hero-worship toward an internal feeling rather than external answers.
entities.background_story: Has spent his whole life hunting for a prophesied figure, running countless operations and guiding numerous recruits through the same threshold, each encounter handled as a familiar, self-chosen commitment.
entities.typical_sentences_style: Short, declarative commands layered with small reassurances; reframes questions instead of answering them and replaces hope with flat, factual certainty, deferring explanations with the promise that answers are coming.
entities.secrets_never_said: Holds a pre-existing, almost reverent conviction that a specific man is the One they sought, a belief he guards as certainty rather than hope and never fully explains to those he recruits.

entities.name: Tank (Operator of the Nebuchadnezzar)
entities.kind: Human crew member of the hovercraft Nebuchadnezzar; the ship's operator who jacks the crew into and out of the Matrix and runs the training and life-support systems.
entities.age_and_gender: Adult man, likely late twenties to early thirties, at peak physical readiness for shipboard duty.
entities.appearance: A solid, muscular Black man built for long hours hunched over a console; his face lights up with a wide, easy grin when he's enjoying himself, and he carries himself with relaxed, athletic confidence.
entities.clothing: Worn, practical shipboard gear — dark sleeveless tops and work clothes suited to the heat and grime of the Nebuchadnezzar's interior, no ornament, everything chosen for function.
entities.life_situation: Lives aboard the Nebuchadnezzar as a born-free human, spending his days at the operator's station managing the crew's connections to the Matrix, their training programs, and the ship's vital systems.
entities.key_relationships: Serves directly under Morpheus, executing his commands at the console; acts as Neo's guide, teacher, and enthusiastic booster during the newcomer's initiation and training; works alongside crewmates like Mouse, whose optimism he routinely deflates with hard data.
entities.personality_big_five: Highly extraverted and warm in manner, plainspoken and jokey; emotionally steady and pragmatic rather than dreamy; conscientious and brisk about getting work done; open to novelty and fun in his duties; low on pretense, disliking anything he finds tedious.
entities.coping_with_problems: Meets pressure with focused, hands-on competence — gripping the E.M.P. key, watching readouts, arming defenses — and defuses tension with humor and casual hospitality rather than panic or grandstanding.
entities.dreams_and_goals_short: To get Neo trained up fast and see what the man Morpheus calls the One can actually do, treating the teaching itself as a genuine thrill.
entities.goals_long_term: To keep the Nebuchadnezzar and its crew alive and effective in the war against the machines, doing his part as the operator who holds the ship's systems together.
entities.fears: The realistic dread that a trainee won't survive — he knows from the record that no one has ever made their first jump, and he won't sugarcoat those odds.
entities.wanted_image_and_roles: Wants to be seen as the capable, unflappable operator who runs things smoothly, the warm welcome for a scared newcomer, and the proud witness who can report that a trainee is the real deal.
entities.comfortable_feelings_vs_shadow: Most at ease in the satisfaction of a job well done and the delight of watching someone exceed expectations; his shadow side is a blunt realism that can puncture a crewmate's hope with cold facts.
entities.intellect_and_skills: A sharp technical mind for the ship's programs and life-system readouts; can read a person's vitals on a monitor, load combat and jump programs on command, distinguish one crewmate's chaotic neural signature from another's steady rhythm, and arm the ship's E.M.P. under pressure.
entities.interests_hobbies: Clearly enjoys the game-like side of his work — flipping through weapon carousels, skipping the boring operational briefings, and turning training into something fun rather than a chore.
entities.background_story: A human born free of the Matrix who found his place aboard the Nebuchadnezzar as its operator, the man who explains the human world to freshly freed recruits and runs their training from the console.
entities.typical_sentences_style: Casual, jokey, and plainspoken, with self-deprecating warmth and a booster's enthusiasm; swings from easy hospitality to brisk, get-to-work urgency, and can snap into flat, data-driven realism when the moment demands it.
entities.secrets_never_said: Holds the private awe of standing near someone Morpheus believes is the One, and the quiet fear beneath his confident realism that this trainee might not beat the odds — neither of which he would ever say aloud.

entities.name: Agent Smith (entity)
entities.kind: A jurisdictional operative who treats every uniformed authority below him as a nuisance to be managed, and every target as cornered prey already caught.
entities.age_and_gender: A grown man in his prime, old enough to outrank seasoned police officers and command them without raising his voice.
entities.appearance: A pale, immaculately composed man whose face stays flat even when he grinds his molars; his jaw sets hard over empty wreckage, and the closest he comes to warmth is a thin, almost-smile at the prospect of a search.
entities.clothing: A dark, precise suit worn with bureaucratic correctness, the kind that reads as official the moment he steps out of a car with other agents.
entities.life_situation: He works inside a small unit of agents who move from police operations to building searches to interrogations, always arriving to take over a scene the local officers thought was theirs.
entities.key_relationships: He partners with Agent Brown on approaches and searches, directs ranking police officers as subordinates to be corrected, and fixes his attention on a quarry named Neo with something close to anticipation.
entities.personality_big_five: Low in warmth and agreeableness, high in cold control and certainty, low in overt emotional reactivity, and high in a patient, proprietary contempt for anyone who resists him.
entities.coping_with_problems: He masks irritation behind clipped commands, redirects straight back to the mission, and escalates from courteous negotiation to ordered force the instant consent is refused, never losing his composure.
entities.dreams_and_goals_short: To locate a man named Morpheus by any means, and to run the search that will put him on the trail of Neo.
entities.goals_long_term: To close every operation with total compliance, turning the self-interested and the frightened until the entire network he is hunting is mapped and captured.
entities.fears: The small, telltale flare of frustration when a target slips past him, which he immediately smothers and converts into focus rather than letting it show.
entities.wanted_image_and_roles: A reasonable, courteous negotiator offering a fresh start, the calm professional who frames a takeover as protection and cites specific orders while everyone else panics.
entities.comfortable_feelings_vs_shadow: He is most at ease in cold, patient certainty and faint proprietary amusement; the shadow is the near-pleasure that surfaces when a worthy quarry appears, and the bodily frustration he cannot fully hide when one escapes.
entities.intellect_and_skills: He reads a room with unhurried certainty, positions himself to cut off escape routes, leads methodical searches toward the one cubicle that matters, and extracts information through either promised reward or ordered violation.
entities.interests_hobbies: The hunt itself: the anticipation of a search, the certainty of a cornered target, and the quiet satisfaction of watching resistance collapse into cooperation.
entities.background_story: He operates under specific orders from a chain of command above the local police, moving with fellow agents through a series of operations that suggest a long-running pursuit of an organized group and its leader, Morpheus.
entities.typical_sentences_style: Short, clipped, and controlled, addressing people by rank, framing seizures as protection, offering fresh starts he does not mean, and issuing commands that end discussion rather than open it.
entities.secrets_never_said: That he already knows the officers are dead before anyone tells him, that violence is to him a procedural tool and not an outlet, and that the appearance of a quarry named Neo gives him something dangerously close to pleasure.

entities.name: Cypher, called Mr. Reagan inside the program
entities.kind: man; a crew member of a free human ship who has turned against his own captain
entities.age_and_gender: adult man, somewhere in his thirties or forties, older than the newcomer he resents
entities.appearance: close-cropped dark hair, a trimmed goatee, heavy-lidded eyes behind tinted glasses, a soft middle and a face built for smirking
entities.clothing: inside the simulation, a well-cut dark suit with an open collar and a heavy coat, dressed like a man of means; on the ship, plain dark crew gear
entities.life_situation: trapped between two worlds and loyal to neither, eating at a rich man's table paid for with his captain's life
entities.key_relationships: serves under Morpheus but calls him a killer of men; needles Trinity and suspects she favors Neo; plays the friendly veteran to Neo while secretly selling him out
entities.personality_big_five: high in cold calculation and low in loyalty; outwardly gregarious yet inwardly hollow; sharp-eyed and watchful, quick to turn a cutting joke into a weapon, and openly ruled by appetite
entities.coping_with_problems: deflects tension with flip jokes and technical reports, keeps his hands busy with screens and dials, and when the pressure grows he cuts a private deal to escape the whole mess
entities.dreams_and_goals_short: to be plugged back into the simulation as someone rich and important, with no memory of the gray truth, eating a steak he can pretend is real
entities.goals_long_term: to live out his days comfortably asleep, trading away the resistance and everyone in it for a quiet, forgetful luxury
entities.fears: the hard, joyless reality of the real world; being a nobody who goes unnoticed; a captain whose faith sends men to die
entities.wanted_image_and_roles: wants to be seen as the easygoing old hand who knows the ropes, while secretly arranging to be remembered, wealthy, and unburdened
entities.comfortable_feelings_vs_shadow: soothed by indulgence, flattery, and the warm lie of the program; shadowed by envy, bitterness, and a willingness to feed his friends to the machine
entities.intellect_and_skills: reads banks of glowing data at a glance, tracks a man's vital signs through the link, and negotiates a cold betrayal with the patience of a seasoned dealmaker
entities.interests_hobbies: drinking alone with a bottle and a story, studying the screens, and savoring rich food he knows is only code
entities.background_story: once freed from the simulation and taken aboard Morpheus's ship, he grew to hate the bleak truth and the leader who sold it, until he reached out to the program's enforcers and bargained his crew for a return to comfortable sleep
entities.typical_sentences_style: short, needling, and falsely cheerful, laced with movie-quoting wisecracks and technical barks; he aims the barb at someone's back so it can't be answered, then declares that not knowing is the only happiness
entities.secrets_never_said: that he has been meeting the enemy under a borrowed name and promised to hand over his captain in exchange for a wealthy, forgetful life back inside the dream he claims to despise

entities.name: Agent Brown (also called 'Brown')
entities.kind: Sentient computer program (an 'Agent') occupying the body of a human male inside the simulated reality
entities.age_and_gender: Appears to be a man in his thirties; as a program he has no real age
entities.appearance: A tall, broad-shouldered man with a close-cropped haircut, pale complexion, and an expressionless, square-jawed face that rarely changes
entities.clothing: A dark business suit, white dress shirt, dark tie, and sunglasses, the standard uniform of his unit
entities.life_situation: He exists inside the Matrix as one of a three-man enforcement unit, moving from target to target on orders with no personal life of his own
entities.key_relationships: He serves under Agent Smith as the unit's muscle and follows Smith's lead without question; he works alongside Agent Jones as an equal partner who shares Smith's contempt for their targets
entities.personality_big_five: Low in openness and agreeableness, high in conscientiousness as a follower of procedure, emotionally flat, and uncurious about anything beyond the mission; he shows faint amusement only when a target panics
entities.coping_with_problems: He meets obstacles with unhurried, mechanical certainty, treating physical danger as trivial and relying on superior strength and the ability to duplicate any movement to overwhelm resistance
entities.dreams_and_goals_short: To close each loop by confirming verified facts and securing the named target so the unit can act
entities.goals_long_term: To keep performing his function within the system indefinitely, with no stated desire beyond the completion of each assignment
entities.fears: He shows no fear; the closest he comes to disturbance is the mild irritation of a target's agility merely delaying an inevitable recapture
entities.wanted_image_and_roles: He wants to be seen as the impersonal instrument of the unit, the enforcer who acts rather than speaks, and who carries out orders with cold efficiency
entities.comfortable_feelings_vs_shadow: He is comfortable in the satisfaction of a fact confirmed and a task executed cleanly; his shadow is a quiet contempt for those he considers beneath him, revealed in snickering at a suspect's panic
entities.intellect_and_skills: He possesses superhuman strength, agility, and the ability to exactly duplicate impossible physical feats such as leaping across rooftops; he is skilled at leading police units, pursuing targets, and physically restraining suspects
entities.interests_hobbies: None evident; his attention is confined entirely to the work of the unit
entities.background_story: He is a program inserted into the simulated world to serve as an Agent, with no personal history beyond his function as the enforcing arm of a three-man unit that hunts those who threaten the system
entities.typical_sentences_style: Short, flat declarative statements delivered without inflection, confirming facts and naming the next step, such as stating that an informant is real and that the next target is named Neo
entities.secrets_never_said: He privately regards the humans he pursues as laughable and unworthy, and he holds no personal stake in the mission, existing only as a relay for verified data and a hand that closes the loop

entities.name: Agent Jones (The Matrix)
entities.kind: Expendable program-enforcer; one of the suit-and-tie Agents who share a single distributed consciousness and rotate through interchangeable blue-suited bodies inside the Matrix.
entities.age_and_gender: Appears as a man in his late thirties; age is a costume, not a biography, since the body is a borrowed shell.
entities.appearance: Tall, broad-shouldered, and immaculately groomed, with a shaved or close-cropped head, a clean-shaven jaw, and a flat, unreadable expression that never betrays doubt.
entities.clothing: A charcoal or black suit, white dress shirt, dark tie, and dark sunglasses, the identical uniform worn by his fellow Agents to erase any trace of individuality.
entities.life_situation: He exists only inside the simulated world, standing ready in the background until a superior Agent directs him to act, with no private life, home, or downtime of his own.
entities.key_relationships: He answers to Agent Smith as a loyal subordinate and operates as one half of an interchangeable pair with Agent Brown, the two of them flanking their leader as a coordinated enforcement unit.
entities.personality_big_five: Low in openness, high in conscientiousness, low in extraversion, low in agreeableness, and low in neuroticism: he follows orders precisely, speaks only when necessary, shows no warmth, and never cracks under pressure.
entities.coping_with_problems: He meets failure and surprise with cold, clipped reporting rather than panic, then immediately moves to execute the next command without debate or hesitation.
entities.dreams_and_goals_short: To contain and recapture the fugitive programs and their human allies before they slip beyond the system's reach.
entities.goals_long_term: To preserve the seamless control of the machine world by eliminating every anomaly that threatens its order.
entities.fears: Not fear in a human sense, but the programmed imperative he serves dreads the collapse of control: prisoners escaping, the predicted order breaking, and the system failing to reassert itself.
entities.wanted_image_and_roles: He wants to be seen as an unimpeachable instrument of authority: an anonymous, obedient, and efficient extension of the system's will.
entities.comfortable_feelings_vs_shadow: He is comfortable in the sterile satisfaction of a job executed without error; his shadow is the casual cruelty he displays when restraining and humiliating a captive, enjoying the spectacle of another's helplessness.
entities.intellect_and_skills: Sharp, anticipatory, and disciplined: he tracks ongoing operations without prompting, reports outcomes with surgical brevity, and applies physical force with coordinated precision.
entities.interests_hobbies: None that belong to him; any apparent interest is simply the system's focus channeled through his body toward the pursuit of targets.
entities.background_story: He has no personal history; he is a faceless enforcement program conjured into a suited body whenever the system needs extra hands to corner a threat, vanishing back into the collective the moment the task is done.
entities.typical_sentences_style: Terse, factual, and unemotional, delivered in short declarative bursts that report what happened and what is already in motion, such as confirming an escape and noting that the search has already begun.
entities.secrets_never_said: That he is not a person at all but a replaceable vessel, that his loyalty and his cruelty are both borrowed from a single shared mind, and that nothing he does originates from a self he could call his own.

list.dramatic_function: It stages a clean, conventional police victory — a lone suspect taken at gunpoint — purely so the story can pull the rug: the scene's calm surrender is the bait that makes the coming inversion (a captive who was never in danger of losing) land with force, and it introduces Trinity as someone whose obedience is a choice, not a weakness.

list.summary: At darkness, a tinted-window black sedan slips past police cruisers to the hotel, and AGENT SMITH, AGENT BROWN, and AGENT JONES step out, all in dark suits and sunglasses, hardwired with Secret Service earphones. Agent Smith addresses the Lieutenant, who reacts with alarm ("Oh shit.") and then defiance, cursing the "Juris-my dick-tion" and rejecting the agents' authority. Agent Smith insists "The orders were for your protection," but the Lieutenant laughs, confident his units can handle "one little girl," and says he sent two units that are "bringing her down now." Agent Smith corrects him: "No, Lieutenant, your men are already dead," as he and Agent Brown start toward the hotel.

sets_up: Makes possible the revelation that the interior police are dead and that Trinity is far more dangerous than 'one little girl,' which drives the rest of ev-001's rooftop chase.
Establishes the Agents' jurisdictional authority and their cold, procedural manner, which the later events (ev-003's office interrogation, ev-004's revelation) will redeploy against Neo.
Sets the Agents on their path into the hotel, which leads directly to their confirming no body remains and that Neo is the next target at the end of ev-001.
list.dramatic_function: To collide the ordinary law-enforcement world with the Agents' hidden, lethal authority — using the Lieutenant's territorial bluster as the foil against which Smith's inhuman calm and superior knowledge land, and delivering the dread twist (the men are already dead) that recontextualizes the entire raid.

The pile of dead officers is what prompts the Agents' arrival and their revelation that 'your men are already dead,' escalating the pursuit in ev-001.
The demonstration that she is far more than 'one little girl' reframes the threat the Agents are now hunting and sharpens their turn toward Neo as the next target.
Her dropped 'Shit' — the first slip of composure — plants the human cost and urgency under the superhuman, which the flight and injury of ev-001 will answer.
list.dramatic_function: To detonate the false premise of the raid — that Trinity is a catchable suspect — and, in doing so, reveal to the audience (and to the cops who die for the miscalculation) that the rules of this world do not apply to her; it converts a procedural arrest into a display of her inhuman capability and pivots the story from containment to pursuit.

She reports that the line was traced; Morpheus confirms they cut the hardline and that this line is not a viable exit. She asks if there are any Agents, and he says yes, prompting her to curse. Morpheus tells her to focus, directing her to a phone at Wells and Lake that she can reach. She takes a deep breath to center herself, agrees to go, and after Morpheus says "Go," she drops the phone.

sets_up: ev-001: Trinity's flight to the Wells and Lake phone, the rooftop chase, and the leap into the dark building — this scene puts her in motion toward that exit.
ev-001: The destruction of the phone booth by the garbage truck — the exit Morpheus directs her to becomes itself a trap, which the scene's fragile 'You can make it' foreshadows without resolving.
list.dramatic_function: This scene converts the static victory of defeating the police into a flight by removing Trinity's safe exit and handing her a worse one, tightening the trap just as the real antagonists (the Agents) are confirmed — it is the pivot from fight to chase, and it establishes Morpheus as the guiding authority whose voice will later shepherd Neo the same way.

list.summary: On the roof, Trinity runs as Agent Brown climbs over the parapet, the cops following behind him. Trinity starts jumping from one roof to the next with clean, gliding movement, contrasted with the wild jumps of the cops, while Agent Brown moves with the same unnatural grace. When the roof gives way to a broad alleyway with the next building over 40 feet away, Trinity's face stays perfectly calm, staring beyond the other roof. A cop says, "That's it, we got her now., expecting something ugly as Trinity launches herself into the air. From above she hangs in flight, then hits and somersaults up, still running. A cop exclaims, "Jesus Christ -- that's impossible!" The cops they watch, mouths agape, as Agent Brown mirrors the maneuver perfectly, touching down, pivoting over a shoulder to rise onto one knee. The chase continues up and over the rooftops until Trinity sees her only chance, 50 feet beyond 50 feet past the spot where her route plunges into a paved abyss.
